---
title: "Schedule"
subtitle: "Two days, about 40% lecture and 60% hands-on"
---

Day 1 ends with every participant having trained and evaluated a model on realistic data. Day 2 moves from building models to using existing ones well, and ends with each group planning an AI project of its own.

## Day 1 — Foundations: data, models and honest evaluation

| Time | Session | Type |
|---|---|---|
| 09:00–09:30 | Welcome and icebreaker: each person names one problem from their work | Discussion |
| 09:30–10:30 | [1. What AI is (and isn't)](modules/01-what-is-ai.qmd) | Lecture |
| 10:30–10:45 | Break | |
| 10:45–12:00 | [2. Data is the foundation](modules/02-data.qmd) | Lecture + lab |
| 12:00–13:00 | Lunch | |
| 13:00–14:15 | [3. Your first models](modules/03-first-models.qmd) | Lab |
| 14:15–14:30 | Break | |
| 14:30–15:30 | [4. Evaluating models honestly](modules/04-evaluation.qmd) | Lecture + lab |
| 15:30–16:15 | [5. Finding structure without labels](modules/05-unsupervised.qmd) | Lab |
| 16:15–16:30 | Wrap-up: "muddiest point" cards | Discussion |

## Shorter and longer formats

The modules are self-contained, so the course scales.

| Format | Keep | Drop or shorten |
|---|---|---|
| Half day (3.5 h) | Modules 1, 4 (as a lecture), 6 (demo only), 8 | All coding labs; no capstone |
| 1 day | Modules 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, and a 45-minute capstone | Modules 5, 7 and 9 become short lecture segments |
| 2 days | Everything (this schedule) | — |
| 6 weekly sessions of 2–3 h | Everything, plus work on participants' own data between sessions | The capstone becomes a final project presented in week 6 |

Labs 02–05 each have three parts: **A** (agronomy), **B** (population genetics) and **C** (metagenomics). With a focused audience, run only the parts that match it.
